newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool indicator rises four cents/kg.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool indicator rises four cents/kg.

text.p: The Australian wool market eastern indicator rose four cents to 556 cents a kg clean at sales in Newcastle, Adelaide and Launceston on Tuesday, Wool International (WI) said in its market report.
Of the 27,124 bales offered, 8.9 percent was passed in.

Japanese and Chinese buyers were principal with support from Taiwanese and Italian operators. In merinos, 19 micron was 2.5 percent dearer, 20/25 0.5 percent dearer, 21/26 one percent dearer, 22 slightly dearer and 23/24 up to 0.5 percent cheaper.
Skirtings were one percent dearer. Crossbreds of 27/28/30 microns were one percent dearer and 29/31 0.5 percent dearer.
In cardings, lambs were unchanged and locks and crutchings were generally unchanged.
Sales continue on Wednesday in Newcastle, Adelaide and Launceston.
